title.en: The Business of Those Who Come After: Seneca's Eighth Letter to Lucilius
title.zh: 为后来的人做事：塞涅卡致卢基里乌斯第八封信

edition.en: The complete letter as given on Latin Wikisource (Epistulae morales ad Lucilium, Liber I), which follows The Latin Library's text; checked against Karl Rudolf Fickert's edition (Leipzig, 1842, volume 1) on the Internet Archive. Section numbers are omitted, the quoted lines of verse are set as quotations, and a missing space is restored.
edition.zh: 全信，据拉丁文维基文库《致卢基里乌斯的道德书信》第一卷（其文本取自 The Latin Library），并与互联网档案馆所藏卡尔·鲁道夫·菲克特校本（莱比锡，1842 年，第 1 卷）核对。节号从略，所引诗句以引文格式排出，并补上一处漏掉的空格。

source.name: Wikisource (la), Epistulae morales ad Lucilium/Liber I

basis.en: Written about 62–64 CE; Seneca died in 65.
basis.zh: 约作于 62—64 年，塞涅卡卒于 65 年。

note.en: Seneca wrote his letters to his friend Lucilius in retirement, and here he answers the charge that withdrawing from public life is idleness: he has shut his door in order to write for posterity, as one would write down a remedy that has worked. The second half turns to the small gift that closes each early letter, a saying of Epicurus, and asks why a good sentence should be thought to belong to anyone. Notice the phrase posterorum negotium ago: he calls it business, not leisure.
note.zh: 塞涅卡给朋友卢基里乌斯写这些信时已经退隐。在这封信里，他回答别人的指责——退出公共生活就是懒散：他关上门，是为了给后世写作，就像把一个有效的药方记下来一样。后半封信转到早期每封信末尾附送的那句格言，这次是伊壁鸠鲁的一句话，并且问：一句好话，为什么要认为它只属于某一个人？请留意 posterorum negotium ago 这个说法：他称之为“事务”，而不是闲暇。

excerpt.orig: Secessi non tantum ab hominibus sed a rebus, et in primis a meis rebus: posterorum negotium ago.
excerpt.en: I have withdrawn not only from people but from affairs, and above all from my own affairs: I am doing the business of those who come after.
excerpt.zh: 我不仅从人群中退了出来，也从事务中退了出来，首先是从我自己的事务中退了出来：我在做的，是后来者的事。

gloss.en: To die in action: the Stoic ideal of staying at one's post to the end.
gloss.zh: 死在行动之中：斯多葛派坚守岗位直到最后的理想。

gloss.en: Favours smeared with birdlime, the sticky paste used to trap small birds.
gloss.zh: 涂了粘鸟胶的恩惠。粘鸟胶是用来捕小鸟的黏胶。

gloss.en: To a court appearance, to stand surety that someone will appear.
gloss.zh: 到法庭去，为某人按期出庭作保。

gloss.en: Fabulae togatae: Roman comedies set in Italy, whose characters wore the toga.
gloss.zh: “穿长袍的戏”，即以意大利为背景、人物穿托加袍的罗马喜剧。

gloss.en: Publilius Syrus, a freed slave who wrote mimes in the first century BCE; his one-line maxims circulated widely.
gloss.zh: 普布利利乌斯·叙鲁斯，公元前一世纪的被释奴隶，写滑稽剧；他的单行格言流传很广。

gloss.en: The barefoot performers of mime as against tragic actors in the high boot, the cothurnus.
gloss.zh: 赤脚的滑稽剧演员，与穿高底靴（cothurnus）的悲剧演员相对。
